articles.title: China's Golden Week reveals cautious consumer spending despite travel surge
articles.summary: Chinese visitors are returning from trips after the 13-day Golden Week holiday. Their subdued spending has raised fresh questions about domestic demand in the world's second-largest economy.

image.caption: Golden Week is typically a time of high levels of travel and spending in ChinaImage: Ryohei Moriya/The Yomiuri Shimbun/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Ya Xi just returned to Shanghai on a red-eye flight after her Golden Week trip to Southeast Asia. "I can stay up all night for a cheaper ticket," she told DW.
She was among the 31.19 million passengers who traveled during the 13-day holiday period that followed the Mid-Autumn Festival on September 25 and China's National Day on October 1.
Many of them spent their budgets more cautiously this year.

"I earn less this year, so I'm lowering my budget for this year's Golden Week," said Xi, who is in her mid-20s. "I spent 5,000 yuan (about €660) on my flight, which was the largest expense of my trip."

Golden Week is viewed as a barometer of the Chinese economy with Beijing using it as an opportunity to showcase the world's second-largest economy's spending power. State media, for instance, reported a record-breaking 25.204 million passenger trips on China's railway network on October 1.

blocks.caption: State media reported record-breaking train passenger numbers over Golden WeekImage: CFOTO/picture alliance

blocks.text: However, early data indicated more moderate spending per traveler and broadly flat passenger traffic, according to Citigroup analysts. Traffic volume during the first four days of the holiday rose just 0.1% year over year, far below the 3.5% increase seen during this year's Labor Day vacation.
Selective spending among younger consumers
Lizzi C. Lee, a fellow on the Chinese Economy at the Asia Society Policy Institute, told DW that Chinese consumers are becoming increasingly selective.
"My read is that people are willing to get out and spend. They're just being much more careful about how much and what they spend on," Lee said.

But being cautious doesn't mean staying frozen, she added. "They'll spend on travel, concerts, restaurants, experiences, and tech… if they think it's worth it, they'll economize pretty aggressively elsewhere."

Xi's Golden Week trip followed this pattern, paying more for significant experiences and economizing elsewhere: "Eat, drink, and be merry," said Xi, indicating she was willing to spend more on food. For example, she set a 200-yuan (about €26) budget for each meal.

blocks.caption: Many Chinese are opting for budget travel options instead of luxury tripsImage: CFOTO/picture alliance

blocks.text: Guo-Chen Wang, an associate research fellow at the Chung-Hua Institution for Economic Research, told DW that the budget-travel trend among Chinese visitors was ongoing.
"The number of trips is increasing, butconsumption remains strained, as I saw in past years," Wang said.

The Chinese government attempted to boost Golden Week spending by providing coupons worth more than 310 million yuan (€41.2 million). Wang remained unconvinced about the effectiveness of such a measure: "That's an old solution to an old problem."
A sign of China's weak domestic demand

It isn't the first Golden Week to see weak consumer demand. During last year's holiday season, the average spending per trip was 911.04 yuan (around €121), the lowest in three years, according to Reuters.
"Beijing still believes the low spending was due to consumers' reluctance [to spend]," Wang said. "In fact, we think Chinese consumers are unable to spend."

While savings kept increasing in Chinese banks, Wang said the vast majority of the savings are held by a small proportion of the population. "In other words, the majority of Chinese people don't have savings."
"The fundamental issue is the wealth gap in Chinese society," he said. "I don't know whether Beijing really neglected this problem or was simply unwilling to face it."
China’s tourism surge: expansion, regulation and challenges

A recent International Monetary Fund publication, Toward a New Economic Growth Model for China, once again noted that China's domestic demand has been weak since the pandemic, when the property market correction began.
Lee, however, saw weak spending during this Golden Week as a confidence problem.

"Theproperty downturnhas hit household wealth, income and job expectations are still pretty soft, and several years of weak prices have trained people to wait for discounts and hunt for value," she told DW.
Tightened cross-border rules played a limited role

Weeks before the Golden Week, China's tightened travel restrictions took effect on September 15. The new restrictions ban citizens from leaving the country if they are deemed to pose a risk to national as well as industrial or technological security.

Wang expected Chinese tourists to turn to domestic travel under the new rules, but the outcome did not match his expectations. "The volume of travel abroad is in fact growing, though not by much," he said.
Lee said she saw little evidence of a broad chilling effect on ordinary outbound tourism, with the Golden Week numbers serving as a "useful reality check."
"The September rules give authorities more room to verify travel purposes and ask for additional information in some cases," Lee said. "They still leave plenty of room for ordinary overseas tourism."
Mi Tang in Taipei contributed to this article.

articles.title: Over 20 Chinese ships spotted in Palawan waters on Wednesday, October 7, 2026 -- PCG
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) observed that there were more than 20 Chinese vessels spotted in the vicinity waters of Pag-asa Island, Palawan on Wednesday, GMA News' Ivan Mayrina reported in "24…

blocks.text: Published October 7, 2026 9:15pm

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) observed that there were more than 20 Chinese vessels spotted in the vicinity waters of Pag-asa Island, Palawan on Wednesday, GMA News' Ivan Mayrina reported in "24 Oras."
The ships that are from the Chinese Maritime Militia and the Chinese Coast Guard were hovering in the island’s waters.
The PCG said they observed that there were more ships earlier and that some already left Pag-asa Island’s waters.
Last month, according to the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), there have been more than 100 Chinese ships recorded within the West Philippine Sea (WPS).

“Month of September, we monitored 101 different vessels ng Coast Guard at ng PLA (People’s Liberation Army) Navy. Ito naman, if we look at it over a longer period of time, let's say six month period kagaya ng first sem assessment natin, na dumami ang kanilang Coast Guard vessels...based on their posture, they will be focusing on enforcing maritime law, 'yung maling pananaw niya sa maritime law, utilizing 'yung China Coast Guard ships para i-push nila ang kanilang mandato,” AFP spokesperson for the WPS Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad said.

(For the month of September, we monitored 101 different vessels of the Coast Guard and of the PLA Navy. Here, if we look at it over a longer period of time, let's say six month period of the first semester assessment, there have been more Coast Guard vessels… based on their posture, they will be focusing on enforcing maritime law, their wrong view of the maritime law, utilizing the Chinese Coast Guard ships to push their mandate.)
Pag-asa Island is a hotspot for these Chinese ships, together with Escoda Shoal and Bajo de Masinloc.
Last week, Chinese Coast Guard vessels blocked Philippine officials from responding to a Chinese fishing vessel performing illegal dynamite fishing at the Sandy Cay near Pag-asa Island.
Meanwhile, PCG Commandant Admiral Ronnie Gil Gavan led the activation of the Coast Guard Auxiliary District in the Kalayaan Island District on Wednesday.
Gavan said that these citizens have an important role in overseeing the country’s sovereignty.
“Hindi tayo nahihinaan ng loob. We will match them hangga't kaya natin. Ship for ship, patrol for patrol. 'Yung mga maling naratibo nila, kino-correct natin sa tamang naratibo,” Trinidad said.
(Our resolve will not weaken. We will match them as much as we can. Ship for ship, patrol for patrol. Their wrong narratives, we will correct it with the right ones.) — Jean Mangaluz/BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Sara, Rodrigo Duterte hid P96M through unutilized manager’s checks — prosecution
articles.summary: Senator-judge Vicente “Tito” Sotto III claims the practice is called 'tinikling' in banking circles

blocks.text: VEEP. Vice President Sara Duterte addresses an event in Pagadian City, Zamboanga del Sur, in late May 2026.
Sara Duterte Facebook page
Senator-judge Vicente “Tito” Sotto III claims the practice is called 'tinikling' in banking circles

items: House prosecutors presented P96 million in manager's checks to establish a pattern of concealment involving Vice President Sara Duterte and former President Rodrigo Duterte.

Bank of the Philippine Islands confirmed a joint time deposit account for the Dutertes, which was opened in 2010 and reached P41.72 million after multiple renewals, with funds later converted into manager's checks.

Senator-judges questioned the relevance of the transactions, with discussions on the practice of leaving manager's checks unutilized, while it was noted that the P96 million was not reflected in the Vice President's Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – House prosecutors on Wednesday, October 7, presented P96 million in manager’s checks as they sought to establish a “pattern of concealment” involving the year-end balances of Vice President Sara Duterte and her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte.

On Day 35 of Duterte’s impeachment trial, Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) division head for central Manila branches Marwin Galvez confirmed the father and daughter had a joint time deposit account opened in January 2010 with a principal amount of P40.65 million.
The account, opened at the BPI-Julia Vargas branch, was renewed 12 times and reached P41.72 million after its final rollover in February 2011.
When the time deposit matured in March 2011, a settlement account was opened and the funds were converted on the same day into a manager’s check for P41.72 million.
Defense lawyer Michael Poa initially objected to the presentation of the bank records, questioning their relevance to the case.
Senator-judge Panfilo “Ping” Lacson then asked the House prosecutors whether they were trying to establish through their direct examination a “pattern aimed at proving concealment.”
Private prosecutor James Bryan Ibrahim Alih answered in the affirmative.
“We wanted to establish a pattern,” Alih said. “Our point is that the manager’s checks being circulated did not reflect on the year-end balance because they were considered ‘floating.’”

In the interjections of Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero, Galvez explained that when a manager’s check is issued, the amount is deducted from the client’s account and transferred to the bank’s settlement account — an account separate from the customer’s account.

The funds will then remain in the settlement account to back the manager’s check while it is unitized. If the manager’s check remains unused for six months, the amount may be returned to the client’s account, Galvez said.

“A similar time deposit that became a manager’s check in the amount of P55 million was also running during the same years, simultaneously with this P41 million. It’s a total of P96 million,” Alih said.
The prosecution presented three more manager’s checks dated April 19, 2012 and October 17, 2012; and October 7, 2013 purchased by the Duterte patriarch. It has a total value of P41.72 million.

Senator-judge Bam Aquino said it was the first time he had heard of such transactions and asked Galvez whether deliberately purchasing manager’s checks and leaving them unutilized was a known practice in banking circles “to keep money.”

Galvez said it was usual for some manager’s checks to be unutilized and requested to be returned. However, he could not determine whether some clients were deliberately purchasing manager’s checks for the purpose of having the funds returned after six months.
“I cannot answer… if some clients are purposely buying manager’s check to return it after six months,” said Galvez.

Senator-judge Vicente “Tito” Sotto III later said the practice is allegedly called “tinikling” in banking circles. Tinikling is a traditional Philippine folk dance wherein a dancer or dancers step, hop, and jump between two moving bamboo poles.

Senator-judge Sherwin Gatchalian said he reviewed Duterte’s Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs) for 2010 and 2011 but did not find the P96-million time deposit accounts in the documents.
Poa came to the defense of Duterte, saying she may have been unaware of the accounts.

“The operative word is if she’s aware… And as we demonstrated during cross, all these time deposits and transactions wala pong prima ng bise presidente (there’s no signature of the Vice President) and all off them were done by the former president,” Poa added.
The Vice President declared zero cash in hand and bank deposits in her SALNs from 2019 to 2024. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Ten people linked to Kenya's first-ever Ebola case quarantined as screening concerns grow
articles.summary: The patient passed through multiple cities in DR Congo, drove to Uganda and eventually flew to Kenya.

blocks.text: Ten people who came into contact with a man who died of Ebola in Kenya have been quarantined, health officials in the East African nation say.
They are also trying to trace 57 other contacts of the Kenyan patient after he travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, dying in hospital in Nairobi on Monday.
This is the East African nation's first-ever Ebola case and there is now growing concern about the country's screening measures.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention chief has told the BBC that despite being sick for a month, the patient passed through multiple cities in DR Congo, driving to Uganda and eventually flying to Kenya without his sickness being detected.

"We know that he left Buta, a city in [northern] DR Congo, to drive to Kisangani. And from Kisangani, he took a flight to Beni. From Beni, he drove to Uganda. And from Uganda, he took a flight to Nairobi," Jean Kaseya told the BBC's Focus on Africa programme.
"What are symptoms he was presenting? Why was he not detected?" he asked.
The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

The current outbreak in DR Congo, which began in May, has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.
Kaseya said the Africa CDC was investigating the case, alongside the Congolese authorities. A team from the organisation was also due to meet the Kenyan health authorities.
Kenya's health ministry official Patrick Amoth said the patient might have passed screening after taking medications that masked his symptoms.
After arriving at the airport in Kenya's capital, he was transferred by a relative to a hospital in the city where he died, and was buried on Tuesday in line with health safety guidelines.
Kenyan authorities have urged people not to panic, with the health ministry assuring of heightened surveillance at airports and border crossings.
But Dr Dennis Miskellah, a representative from Kenya's main doctors' union, said the Ebola case did not come as a surprise to him and most health workers.
He told the BBC's Newsday programme that he had witnessed "lapses" at various border points, including with neighbouring Uganda and Tanzania, as well as at Kenyan's main airport.

"How could you have been sick for almost a month plus in DR Congo, come all the way to the country through not just any small border point, but the main entry point, the main gateway into the country and pass unnoticed?
"That's the question that most Kenyans are asking."
The health ministry says it has intensified measures to contain the spread, with a joint response involving county administrations, humanitarian partners and others.
President William Ruto has said that surveillance and rapid response teams are on the ground, building on the systems that the country adopted following the outbreak in DR Congo in May.
His spokesman said Kenya had the capacity to detect, isolate and manage suspected cases, adding that so far more than 650,000 travellers had been screened and 267 samples tested.
Facilities in four main hospitals have been designated for the management of Ebola patients, including at the Nairobi Hospital, where the first Ebola patient died.

In June, a US plan to establish an Ebola treatment facility at a military base in the central Kenyan town of Nanyuki sparked concern, with Kenyans reacting furiously about the risks of cross-border infection. The plan was halted by the courts.

On Wednesday, Health Minister Aden Duale told local television station NTV that pending the outcome of the court case, the government was considering turning the facility into the "first" infectious disease hospital in the region, to deal with outbreaks like Ebola.
More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak of the disease.
Shortly after DR Congo declared an outbreak of Ebola in May, it was also reported in Uganda, where two people died.
However, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that county free of the disease in August.
On Tuesday, Uganda's health ministry emphasised that the country remained free of Ebola and was continuing to "maintain strong surveillance measures to protect public health".
It said the Kenyan Ebola patient had transited through the country for less than 24 hours and screening teams had "observed he had a normal temperature at the time of departure".
According to Africa CDC chief, his organisation was working with all the countries in the region to reinforce response mechanisms.
Kasiye said Kenya was "well prepared" and was therefore able to immediately receive the case, "but it is not the case for all other countries".
"It means the regional approach is more important today to stop this outbreak."
However, Kasiye said there was no quick testing available at border points and the taking of temperatures was unreliable as medication is able to stop a fever.
"I have to make it clear - we don't have diagnostics to test for Ebola. It's just about temperature," he said.

Dr Miskellah, from the Kenyan doctors' union, said he was concerned that governments were counting on the "honesty and full co-operation of the travellers to self-declare, to say the truth" about their health.
This was however undermined by a lack of proper health education to destigmatise the virus, meaning people often wanted to hide their symptoms, he said.

articles.title: German spy scandal threatens national security
articles.summary: The arrest of Germany's former intelligence chief August Hanning could undermine national security, experts warn, as allies may reconsider their intelligence relationships.

image.caption: The arrest of August Hanning, former president of Germany's foreign intelligence service, the Bundesnachrichtendienst (BND), is threatening to cause a major rupture in Germany's intelligence relationshipsImage: Sebastian Gollnow/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The arrest of August Hanning, former president of Germany's foreign intelligence service, the Bundesnachrichtendienst (BND), and his former chief-of-staff, Manfred D.*, is threatening to cause a major rupture in Germany's intelligence relationships, according to analysts, as the full scale of the scandal begins to be understood abroad.

Manfred D. is accused of having sold around 2,000 highly classified documents to Hanning over a period of 12 years, long after the latter stepped down from the BND in 2005, after seven years as its chief. Manfred D. continued to serve all of Hanning's successors, including the current BND chief Martin Jäger, before retiring in March this year.
On one occasion, the state prosecutor said, Hanning "used classified intelligence provided by Manfred D. to draft an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service."
DW's Michaela Küfner looks at Germany's espionage scandal

According to Florian Flade, reporter for public broadcaster ARD, most of these documents were weekly intelligence briefings delivered to the German government by the BND, including the latest findings from partner intelligence agencies in other countries.

"This is very, very sensitive because it involves partner agencies in other countries," Flade told DW's Berlin Briefing podcast. "And we heard this also involves information about the Iranian nuclear program, the Russian military, also the Ukraine war."
Broken trust, broken credibility

Some pundits now say that the biggest concern is what conclusions the intelligence agencies of allied countries will draw from this affair. In the past, the US CIA is known to have shared information on radical Islamists in Germany, which possibly helped to prevent terrorist attacks in the country.

If it now emerges that information was leaving the BND via Hanning, that relationship could be undermined, particularly if it was also eventually ending up in the hands of the intelligence agencies of Russia and China (though there is no suggestion of that as yet).

"There's huge damage being done not only to the outer appearance and image of the BND," said Flade. "There's a damage assessment now happening within the BND. Also, they're talking to partners about this because they want to know if their information was given to other countries."

That could also potentially have consequences for Germany's national security in the growing confrontation with Russia. The BND, which is currently subject to more legal restrictions than other intelligence agencies around the world, considers its relationship with its US counterpart as vital.

"There might be a change in the amount of information that is coming from the US and others," Flade added, though ultimately, he pointed out, it might be difficult for the BND to know what they're not being told.
Security loopholes in Germany's parliament spark concern

Only a day before the scandal broke, current BND President Martin Jäger reiterated his concern that Germany could slide into a military conflict with Russia, telling a parliamentary hearing that the Kremlin was already waging a "shadow war," and that further military rearmament was "unfortunately necessary" — though he did say that there was currently no indication of active preparations from Russia.

Flade said that, behind the scenes, Jäger is furious about the leak of information from Manfred D., and called a meeting on Tuesday of all BND officials to underline the how serious the consequences of sharing information could be. New internal security measures are also being put in place.

The new case could not have come at a worse time for Jäger or the BND. For one thing, new laws are currently being prepared to expand the agency's powers, partly to improve the BND's standing among its foreign partners.

For another thing, another BND agent, Carsten L. and a businessman named Arthur E., are currently on trial in Berlin on treason charges for passing on classified documents to the Russian secret service in 2022.

blocks.caption: Florian Flade is an espionage expert and guest in DW's Berlin Briefing podcast this weekImage: DW

blocks.text: New rules for old officials?

The case has also raised questions about what former intelligence officials should and shouldn't be allowed to do once they leave office. Hanning founded his own security consultancy business after he left the BND, for which he apparently used his contacts and knowledge to advise his clients. This is legal and tolerated, but many think it shouldn't be.

Timo Lange, of the NGO LobbyControl, said that the Hanning case shows why former intelligence officials must be prevented from working as security consultants in any capacity for the rest of their lives.

"It is fundamentally problematic when high-ranking officials from the intelligence or military sectors, after leaving government service, act as consultants for various — and in some cases unknown — clients from abroad," Lange said in a statement. "This is an obvious gateway for illegitimate foreign influence and jeopardizes the security interests of Germany and the European Union."

But as Flade pointed out, Hanning's career path is not exactly unusual. "These people are trying to just make some money with what they can do best, which is networking and then selling the security assessments that they do," he said. "And yeah, working for companies or even for other countries as a consultant."
Edited by Rina Goldenberg

Editor's note: DW follows the German press code, which stresses the importance of protecting the privacy of suspected criminals or victims and urges us to refrain from revealing full names in such cases.

articles.title: Sara Duterte denies hand in joint bank account with dad Rodrigo
articles.summary: The defense panel on Wednesday said Vice President Sara Duterte does not recall having or participating in transactions involving a joint Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) account under her name…

blocks.text: The defense panel on Wednesday said Vice President Sara Duterte does not recall having or participating in transactions involving a joint Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) account under her name and that of her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, which was supposedly used to purchase a P41.7-million manager’s check.

Defense counsel Michael Poa made the statement on Day 35 of the impeachment trial after Senator-Judge Risa Hontiveros asked whether the flagged P41.7-million manager’s check was owned and controlled by Rodrigo Duterte, and not the Vice President.
“To better phrase it, our client does not have any recollection of this account,” Poa said, adding that the matter was only raised during a previous hearing of the House Quad Committee.

“Nung lumabas ang mga accounts, tinitignan namin itong mga accounts na ito and I was asked by the Vice President to verify kasi hindi niya natatandaan na may ganitong account at wala daw siyang transaksyon,” he added.
(When these accounts surfaced, we examined them, and the Vice President asked me to verify them because she did not recall having such an account and said she had no transactions involving it.)
If that is the case, Hontiveros asked whether the Vice President was attributing the flagged transactions solely to her father.
“Ang sinasabi lang po niya ay wala siyang naging partisipasyon dito,” Poa answered.
(What she is saying is that she had no participation in these.)
The defense counsel also said they did not wish to prejudice the former president or his counsel regarding whatever legal defenses they may have concerning the accounts.
The prosecution earlier flagged a P41.7-million manager’s check linked to Rodrigo and Sara Duterte that was supposedly “floating” for years and was not reflected in year-end balances.

A prosecution witness, BPI division head for Central Manila branches Marwin Galvez, confirmed the existence of a joint peso time deposit opened on January 22, 2010, at the bank’s Julia Vargas Branch in Pasig City under the name “Rodrigo Roa Duterte or Rodrigo Roa Duterte and Sara Z. Duterte,” with a principal amount of P40.65 million.
Galvez said the time deposit had 12 rollover periods or renewals. At the last renewal in February 2011, the amount had increased to P41.7 million, including interest.

The witness said that in March 2011, a credit and debit memo showed that a manager’s check worth P41.7 million was purchased. The manager’s check, however, remained unutilized after its six-month validity period.

The transaction was among the financial records being presented in support of Article 2 of the Articles of Impeachment, which centers on the allegation that Duterte accumulated unexplained wealth and failed to fully disclose her assets and interests in her SALNs.

Private prosecutor James Bryan Alih said the prosecution intended to prove a “pattern,” in which a transaction in 2011 moved around for several more years and was later used to purchase insurance policies.

Responding to an inquiry by Senator-Judge Francis Pangilinan, Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero confirmed that while the signature of the Vice President did not appear in any transaction involving account ending in 9539.

"We confirm, as well, the statement made by Attorney James that the signature of the Vice President appears in the document that opened the account, as well as in the signature sheet or KYC (know-your-client) documents for July 2020 and July 25, 2017.
The signature of the Vice President also appears in the KYC document for June 13, 2023, Escudero said.
'Why involve Rodrigo?'
In his interjection, Senator-Judge Robin Padilla questioned the repeated mention of former President Rodrigo Duterte’s name during Galvez’s direct examination.

“Kanina pa po kasi nababanggit ang pangalan ng dating Pangulong Rodrigo Roa Duterte. Hindi ko alam bakit kailangang idamay pa dito ang matanda. Masasabi po niyan, may ginawa bang kalokohan ’yung matanda?” Padilla asked.
(The name of former President Rodrigo Roa Duterte has been mentioned repeatedly. I don’t know why it is necessary to drag the old man into this. Did the old man do anything wrong?)
The bank official answered, “Not in the documents that we submitted, Your Honor.”— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: France suspends use of stun grenades against protesters
articles.summary: France is suspending the use of stun grenades against protesters as allegations of student brutality draw more anger. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is also set to address the nation later this…

image.caption: Police have fired tear gas to break up demonstrations in several French cities since protests beganImage: Fred Tanneau/AFP

blocks.text: France is suspending the use of stun grenades at student-led protests as people report allegations of police brutality at demonstrations that have widened over the weeks.
"I am suspending their use in the high school student protests until the facts of the incident have been clarified," Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told RTL radio broadcaster on Wednesday.
He emphasized that the suspension was "only for the high school student protests" and for "just long enough to understand what happened."
Nunez announced the measure to curb growing anger after reports about teenagers having lost their hands or teeth during protests drew anger.

French regional newspaper La Voix du Nord reported this Monday that a 15-year-old had his hand and a part of his lower arm blown off after picking up a police stun grenade that then detonated during protests.
Last week, a 14-year-old student in northwest Paris was hit in the jaw as a tear gas canister was fired during protests, with the officer having been charged on Tuesday.
The order also comes before an address by Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu to protesters later Wednesday evening.
More to follow.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro’s advance in Brazil’s election is grim jolt for climate campaigners
articles.summary:
Inquest under way into why President Lula’s success in curbing Amazon deforestation has not lead to success at polls

More fire, more ash, more crime, more death. And a globally important…

blocks.text: More fire, more ash, more crime, more death. And a globally important ecosystem driven ever more rapidly towards a point of no return. That is the prospect for the Amazon rainforest for at least the next four years if Flávio Bolsonaro holds on to the lead he established this week in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election.
This appears to be of far more concern to the outside world than to voters in Latin America’s biggest, richest and most biodiverse nation.

The far-right son of the former president and jailed coup-monger Jair Bolsonaro won 47% of the vote, putting him in pole position before the 25 October runoff with the incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who was backed by 44.2%.

The result is an unnerving jolt to climate and nature campaigners. Taken out of context, this appears to be a vote against the forest. The current administration of Lula (as the veteran Brazilian president is best known) has reduced deforestation in the Amazon by almost 50%. But that success secured little noticeable electoral traction for either Lula or pro-forest candidates in other polls held the same day. The former environment minister Marina Silva lost a bid for the Senate and Joenia Wapichana, a former head of Brazil’s Indigenous affairs agency, Funai, failed to win a seat in Congress. Out of 57 Indigenous candidates, only two won.

blocks.caption: Flavio Bolsonaro has shown he is as willing as his father, Jair, to curb nature protections and allow Indigenous territories to be exploited. Photograph: Jorge Sáenz/AP

blocks.text: Flávio Bolsonaro is the heir to the political legacy of his father, Jair Bolsonaro, a former army captain whose four years in power resulted in a 59.5% increase in Amazon deforestation, roughly equivalent to destroying 2bn trees.

If he wins, Bolsonaro has promised to free his father, who was imprisoned for plotting a military coup and attempting to annihilate democracy in Brazil. He has said that his father could have any position he wants in his administration.

Flávio Bolsonaro has shown that he will be just as willing as his father to dismantle protections for climate and nature and allow illegal miners, loggers and land grabbers to invade Indigenous territories. As a lawmaker, he backed a 2019 bill to eliminate requirements for landowners in the Amazon to conserve a proportion of native vegetation. In his manifesto, he completely ignored the climate crisis. And he has courted support from some of the most predatory landowners in the rainforest.

blocks.caption: Lula’s social media campaign has not been as effective as that of the Bolsonaro team.  Photograph: Evaristo Sa/AFP/Getty

blocks.text: He is also part of a movement – Bolsonarism – that is geared towards maximising profits for extractive industries regardless of the environmental cost. Take its victorious candidate for the Amazonian state of Pará, Daniel Santos, who was fined $275,000 (£208,000) for deforestating 280 hectares (692 acres) of his land without authorisation and is now promising to waive such penalties. As a result of Sunday’s election, Bolsonarists now control seven of the nine states in the Brazilian Amazon, and could win an eighth in the runoffs.

Bolsonarist influence in the legislature, which is dominated by agribusiness interests, is also growing. Jair’s brother, Eduardo, and mother-in-law, Michelle, were elected to the Senate, while an uncle and brother won seats in the lower house of deputies. Even before the election, Congress had been pushing hard to weaken environmental protections. Now it will be almost impossible to stop, particularly given the current chaos in the supreme court, which has been a partial check on untrammelled expansion by miners, ranchers and monoculturalists. Against these forces, Lula would struggle to govern even if he wins the runoff.

blocks.caption: A Flavio Bolsonaro supporter rides in a truck decorated with campaign stickers for the far-right presidential candidate at a rally in Goiania, Goias state. Photograph: Sérgio Lima/AFP/Getty

blocks.text: As a result, it is not just the Amazon that is in peril, but all of Brazil’s biomes, its traditional peoples and the stability of the global climate. The question now is why voters paid so little heed to these concerns.

That inquest is already under way. Many focus on the influence of social media, which has been used far more effectively by the far right. During the Bolsonaro administration, his sons were part of the “hate cabinet” that spread fear and disinformation via WhatsApp groups and other online channels – Bolsonaro’s second son, Carlos, was indicted by federal police for leading the group. Environmentalists were often the target.

Another factor is the expansion of US-style Pentecostalism, which is steadily supplanting Catholicism across Brazil, particularly in the Amazon. The political and environmental consequences of that religious shift can be seen by comparing the pro-nature treatise of the past two popes with the sermons of many evangelical preachers who encourage followers to seek wealth today as much as, if not more, than following moral creeds to ensure a good afterlife.

Lula, 80, has been slow to adapt. Although he is arguably the most iconic and successful Latin American politician of the 21st century, his messaging seems less attuned to the people than it was in his heyday. The Workers party has struggled in an era of weaker unions and in some ways been the victim of its own success – with education and social policies that raised millions out of poverty and created greater expectations for consumption and entrepreneurism; and huge subsidies to farmers, who now support the right wing because they chaff at environmental limits.

blocks.caption: A woman looks at posters depicting the former president Jair Bolsonaro, alongside the words: ‘Remember that?’ Photograph: Pilar Olivares/Reuters

blocks.text: Tied into those explanations are the geopolitics of the climate and nature crisis, which is exacerbating great power rivalry between the US and China and amplifying extreme ideologies as much as extreme weather. In this light, the Brazil election is just the latest in a broader pattern of the far right taking control to expand extractivism despite growing evidence that the capitalist economy is breaking planetary boundaries. In the past two years, Donald Trump has ripped apart environmental regulations in the US and treated the rest of the Americas as his sphere of influence. Argentina was already onboard. Venezuela has been invaded for its resources, while in Colombia, Peru and Chile there has been a sharp shift to the right.

Will Brazil be the next domino to fall to Trumpism and its bonfire approach to nature? The Bolsonaro family certainly hope so. Jair went so far as to salute the US flag. His son Eduardo urged the US to apply tariffs on Brazilian people to “punish” the government for imprisoning his father. The Brazilian intelligence agency has warned that the US was trying to interfere in the election.

That election isn’t over yet. Lula stands a small chance if he can win over the many millions of voters who chose not to mark their ballots for either candidate. But the odds are stacked against him. Most of the eliminated candidates were on the right so their supporters are more likely to switch to Bolsonaro. No first round leader has ever failed to win the runoff of a Brazilian presidential election.

Voters, of course, are allowed to change their minds. Either on 25 October or, constitutionally, in four years’ time. But for how much longer will that be possible? If Bolsonaro wins, it won’t just be Lula that is finished, it could also be the Amazon and democracy itself.

articles.title: Anyare? Villars’ AllHome, AllDay confirm store closures
articles.summary: From a peak of 72 stores two years ago, AllHome is down to 34 stores, while the store count of AllDay drops from 40 to 13, as of September 2026

blocks.text: From a peak of 72 stores two years ago, AllHome is down to 34 stores, while the store count of AllDay drops from 40 to 13, as of September 2026

items: AllHome and AllDay, retail companies owned by the Villar family, are experiencing significant declines in their number of outlets.
Both companies cited the need to improve operational efficiency and profitability.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – From fast-growing just a few years ago to fast-declining.

Villar-owned retail companies AllHome and AllDay confirmed on Wednesday, October 7, the decline in their number of outlets in light of recent financial troubles and stiff competition, in separate disclosures to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE).
The Villars’ home improvement brand AllHome said its total store count stood at 34 as of September 29, 2026, down 26% from 47 as of December 31, 2025.
Based on AllHome’s annual reports it had 15 stores in 2016, 18 in 2017, 23 in 2018, 45 in 2019, 50 in 2020, 57 in 2021, 60 in 2022, 72 in 2023, and still 72 in 2024.
From its peak in 2023 and 2024, the number of AllHome stores has dropped by 81%.

blocks.caption: Rappler graphic based on AllHome annual reports and Philippine Stock Exchange disclosures

blocks.text: “The company confirms that it has closed certain stores as part of its store network optimization program. These measures are intended to improve operating efficiency and support long-term profitability within its existing retail business,” AllHome said.
The company, which started in 2013 with four stores and debuted in the PSE in 2019, said it “remains engaged in its core retail business.”
AllHome has three categories for AllHome stores: large mall-based, large free-standing, and small specialty.

“The company continues to operate its remaining store network. The company’s store closures and resizing of underperforming locations are intended to optimize productivity and maintain a more efficient cost structure,” it added.

“Store operations have been realigned based on sales throughput, customer traffic, and operational requirements, allowing the company to right-size manpower and reduce excess costs while maintaining service quality and operational effectiveness.”
AllHome had a net loss of P36.4 million from January to September 2025, and a net profit of P384 million in the same period in 2024, based on unaudited annual reports.
The PSE had asked AllHome and AllDay to respond to news reports that the Gokongwei Group’s Shopwise would soon take over the space of AllHome at Vista Mall in Santa Rosa City, Laguna.

blocks.caption: STILL OPEN. The AllHome store at the Villar family’s Vista Mall, Santa Rosa City, Laguna, on October 4, 2026. Photo by Leanne Jazul/Rappler
PRICE DROP. Shoppers visit the AllHome store offering a ‘Price Drop’ at Vista Mall in Santa Rosa City, Laguna, on October 4, 2026. Photo by Leanne Jazul/Rappler

blocks.text: Rappler’s photo editor Leanne Jazul was in the area on Sunday, October 4, and was able to take photos of the retail outlet. One of his photos shows AllHome having a “Price Drop” sale.

blocks.caption: [Vantage Point] The road to plenty: Four titans and the battle for the Santa Rosa peso

blocks.text: With respect to its grocery brand AllDay Marts, the separate Villar company said its total store count was 13 as of September 29, 2026, down 50% from 26 as of December 31, 2025.

blocks.caption: CLOSED. A shuttered AllDay Convenience Store in Antipolo City, Rizal, in November 2025. Photo by Isagani de Castro Jr./Rappler

blocks.text: AllDay, which was incorporated in December 2016, said the company “remains engaged in its core grocery retail business,” and that it would “continue to operate its remaining store network.”
“The closure of certain stores…is aimed at improving the company’s long-term profitability, overall operational efficiency, and aligning store network with market conditions,” it added.
Based on AllDay annual reports, it had a peak of 40 stores in 2023 and 2024. Thus, its number of stores has fallen by 67%.

blocks.caption: Rappler graphic based on AllDay Marts annual reports, corporate disclosures, and press release

blocks.text: AllDay disclosed a net profit of P369 million as of December 2023, which fell 27% to P268 million as of December 2024. Sales also fell 9.2% from P10.1 billion in December 2023 to P9.25 billion in December 2024. It said this was “brought about by low-performing stores where there is intense market competition.”

On Wednesday, AllDay said that in order “improve profitability,” it would “optimize its supermarket operations by selectively adopting smaller mini-mart formats to enhance operational efficiency and better serve its target market.”

“The company will also focus on cost discipline, and active liquidity management, including working capital optimization and prudent cash prioritization — while maximizing the value of its existing footprint to restore sustainable profitability,” it said.

blocks.caption: HAKOT. Shoppers take advantage of AllDay Supermarket’s ‘Hakot Sale’ in select stores in Metro Manila, Calabarzon, and Pampanga, based on photos posted online by the retail chain. Photo from AllDay Supermarket’s Facebook page

blocks.text: Last July 2, AllDay Supermarket’s official Facebook account posted an “AllDay Payday Hakot Sale” with steep discounts ranging from 50% to 75% on selected items at its stores in Mandaluyong City; Taguig City; Santa Rosa City, Laguna; General Trias City, Cavite; and in Pampanga. The posts also showed consumers taking advantage of the sale, filling up grocery carts with various discounted items.
The president and chief operating officer of AllHome and also of all AllDay resigned last year amid a drop in corporate earnings, as disclosed in September 2025.

AllHome and AllDay chairman Manny Villar had reported record sales for AllDay in 2021 or five years ago, describing it as “stellar” and “consistent performance.” (READ: Tracking the fallout of Manny Villar’s spot in Forbes’ list of richest individuals)

In the same release five years ago, then-AllValue president and now-senator Camille Villar said AllDay’s growth since it started operations was “a product of our propensity to innovate and remain on the cutting edge of retail consumer trends.”
She added, “AllDay has and will always continue to innovate to stay a step ahead of the local supermarket landscape.”

Retail was seen as complementary to the Villars’ housing projects, having built over 500,000 homes that made it the “largest homebuilder” in the country. This “synergy,” AllHome said in its 2022 annual report, gave “AllHome easy access to a captive market and ideal locations in growing residential communities nationwide, enabling its rapid store network growth.”
In 2025, Rappler published this exclusive report on some suppliers of the Villars’ coffee retail brand Coffee Project not getting paid on time. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Germany: Ex-spy chief sent to pretrial detention on treason charges
articles.summary: August Hanning has been remanded into pretrial detention after his Tuesday arrest. The case has prompted calls for transparency when spies leave the government.

image.caption: Germany's ex-spy chief August Hanning appeared at the Federal District Court in Karlsruhe on WednesdayImage: Uli Deck/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Former German foreign intelligence agency boss August Hanning appeared before a federal judge in the western city of Karlsruhe on Wednesday following his arrest on espionage and treason charges Tuesday.
He has been ordered to remain in detention ahead of his trial.
Manfred D., Hanning's former chief of staff at the Bundesnachrichtendienst (BND), was also detained.
What are the charges against Hanning?

He is accused of having stolen secret documents and turned these over to Hanning, who, as a private-sector security advisor, in turn reportedly sold the secret documents to an as yet unnamed foreign spy agency or agencies.
Nouripour: Hanning arrest a 'huge success'

It is estimated that the two stole and potentially passed on more 2,000 secret documents between 2010 and 2023. Federal investigators say it is unclear how much information was stolen and to whom it was sold.
Hanning ran Germany's BND intelligence service from 1998 until 2005 before becoming state secretary at the Federal Interior Ministry and then entering private business as a security advisor.

The issue has raised serious questions about the trustworthiness of Germany's intelligence agencies and shocked politicians into action as they claim not enough is being done to make sure that high-ranking security officials are not abusing their experience when transitioning to jobs in the private sector.
DW's Michaela Küfner looks at Germany's espionage scandal

articles.title: Nobel chemistry prize goes to pair who solved mystery of ‘mirror image’ molecules
articles.summary: This year's prize was awarded for discoveries that showed how chemical reactions can be driven to favor a single molecular mirror image, work that has been key for chemists who design reactions for…

blocks.text: STOCKHOLM, Sweden – Scientists Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for solving a long-standing riddle of asymmetric “mirror image” molecules, a discovery hugely important for pharmaceutical manufacturing, the award-giving body said on Wednesday, October 7.
Soai, 76, is Japanese, and Kagan, 95, is French, and their work built on a discovery by the 19th century French chemist Louis Pasteur.

“This is the most exciting day in my life, I am very glad to share this prize with professor Henri Kagan,” Soai said, speaking by phone to the Nobel Prize press conference, adding he had been out shopping when receiving the news.
The Nobel committee was still trying to contact Kagan to inform him of the award.
The chemistry Nobel, always the third prize to be awarded during Nobel week, followed those for medicine and physics announced on Monday and Tuesday.

Many of the molecules essential to life exist in two forms that are mirror images of each other, like left and right hands. Yet living organisms almost exclusively use only one version, a phenomenon known as “homochirality” — from the Greek word for hand — that has puzzled chemists for more than a century.

This year’s prize was awarded for discoveries that showed how chemical reactions can be driven to favor a single molecular mirror image, work that has been key for chemists who design reactions for the manufacture of pharmaceuticals.

“The left-handed version of the drug can have one effect, and the right-handed version can have another effect, and then we need methods for selectively preparing them,” Peter Somfai, a member of the Nobel Committee for Chemistry, said.
“In developing such methods the findings of this year’s laureates are important. They provided powerful tools for that,” he said.
The first link in the chain in solving the problem was work by Pasteur, who died before the Nobel Prizes were first awarded.

He was looking at tartaric acid, important in the production of wine, and noticed that bacteria only ferment one of the two forms of tartaric acid — that which is naturally found in grapes. With the other there is no fermentation.
That proved that some substances occur in two forms and that they have different properties, sometimes very damaging to health.
How to create the right form of a chiral substance was a problem not solved until Kagan and Soai were able to produce asymmetric reactions, creating an excess of one form.
The importance of the work is illustrated by the case of the thalidomide scandal in the early 1960s, when thousands of children were affected by birth defects caused by a sedative, thalidomide.
When researchers analysed what had happened, they realized that it was the active substance’s mirror image that caused the harm.

Established in the will of Swedish inventor and businessman Alfred Nobel, the prizes for achievements in science, literature and peace have been awarded since 1901, with a few interruptions mostly due to the world wars.

Nobel, a chemist by trade, amassed huge wealth in the 19th century from inventions primarily tied to warfare, most notably dynamite. The economics prize is a later addition funded by the Swedish central bank.

Sometimes overshadowed by more famous laureates in the fields of physics, literature and peace, the chemistry awards have still recognized many influential discoveries such as nuclear fission and genetic sequencing techniques.

Last year’s chemistry award went to scientists Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi for the development of so-called metal–organic frameworks, molecular constructions that can help tackle challenges such as climate change and lack of fresh water.

The laureates will receive their medals from Sweden’s King Carl XVI Gustaf at a ceremony in Stockholm on December 10, the anniversary of Alfred Nobel’s death. The awards are followed by a lavish banquet at Stockholm City Hall.
They also share 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million), as well as the fame of winning arguably the world’s most prestigious science award.
The peace prize, the only Nobel not presented in Sweden, is awarded separately in Oslo. – Rappler.com
($1 = 10.0309 Swedish crowns)

articles.title: Jonvic Remulla congratulates Harold Respicio on negative drug results
articles.summary: Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla congratulated Reina Mercedes, Isabela Vice Mayor Harold Respicio, on the negative results of the latter's drug test. Respicio had himself checked for illegal drugs…

blocks.text: Published October 7, 2026 7:32pm
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla congratulated Reina Mercedes, Isabela Vice Mayor Harold Respicio, on the negative results of the latter's drug test.
Respicio had himself checked for illegal drugs after Remulla said he wanted the vice mayor to undergo a drug test after he got into a shouting match with barangay officials in Reina Mercedes.
"Congratulations," Remulla said.
"Now that it's confirmed that he's not on shabu, totoo na talaga na natural ang sayad ng utak niya," he added.
Remulla said he would leave it to provincial officials to deal with Respicio, but suggested that the vice mayor undergo a drug test, citing his behavior during the heated session.
“But [Governor Rodolfo Albano is] handling him. I advise him to give him a drug test kasi mukhang adik yung asal niya eh (because he's acting like an addict)," he said.
Remulla expressed dismay over Respicio's behavior. Under the law, the DILG exercises a supervisory role over local governments.
"Meron bang normal na vice mayor na ganun? Parang wala sa sarili eh. Di ba? Parang hindi halal,” he added.
(Is there a normal vice mayor who acts like that? He seems out of his mind. Right? He does not act like an elected official.)
Remulla said the DILG is also studying the possible issuance of a show-cause order requiring Respicio to explain his actions.
He said the incident may also involve alleged abuse against a person in authority after Respicio reportedly shouted at a police officer.
In a phone interview with GMA News' Jun Veneracion, Respicio said he was ready to accept Remulla's challenge to undergo a drug test.
Respicio responded to Remulla, daring the DILG chief to a live, joint drug test at the hospital.
“Secretary Jonvic, magpa-drug test tayo now. Live! Exclusive! Samahan mo ko sa St. Luke’s, now! Today! Tignan natin kung nagdru-drugs si Atty. Harold Respicio,” Respicio said in a social media video.
(Secretary Jonvic, let's take a drug test now. Live! Exclusive! Join me at St. Luke's, now! Today! Let's see if Atty. Harold Respicio is on drugs.)
Following his release of the negative results, the vice mayor called out Remulla over the expense incurred for the testing.
“Jonvic, i-refund mo ko. Ang mahal ng drug test,” Respicio said.
(Jonvic, refund me. Drug tests are expensive.) —NB, GMA News

articles.title: PSC steps in as Asian Tour’s 108th Philippine Open dangles $1 million
articles.summary: The Philippine Sports Commission helps salvage Asia's oldest national golf championship as Filipino golfer Miguel Tabuena headlines the local cast

blocks.text: SWING. Filipino golfer Miguel Tabuena in action.
PHOTO RELEASE
The Philippine Sports Commission helps salvage Asia's oldest national golf championship as Filipino golfer Miguel Tabuena headlines the local cast

items: The 108th Philippine Open will take place at Manila Southwoods from November 12, with a $1 million prize pool provided by the Philippine Sports Commission.
The tournament, which has a rich history dating back to 1913, aims to showcase top local and international talent, including past champions like Miguel Tabuena and Angelo Que.
Despite challenges such as the withdrawal of a title sponsor, the Asian Tour and local golf authorities are committed to ensuring the event proceeds successfully.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Some of the biggest names on the Asian Tour — and the brightest talents the Philippines can offer — set out to win Asia’s oldest national golf championship when Manila Southwoods, which is being spruced up to perfect championship shape, hosts the 108th playing of the Philippine Open in just over a month.

The Philippine Sports Commission (PSC) has stepped in to make sure that the event will be one to remember, putting up a $1 million (around P63 million) kitty for the 72-hole championship beginning November 12 at the world-class Masters course of the SW complex in Carmona, Cavite.

“It is a tradition that the PSC certainly wants to continue with,” PSC Chairman Patrick Gregorio said after making the pledge to make the tournament a big Asian Tour leg. “We wouldn’t want such a big event be put on the shelf.
“It’s the Philippine Open, it’s the pride of the country.”

The Open first came to being in 1913 and has been held yearly save for seven times, the first being in 2003 because of a name dispute, the next two in 2013 and 2016 because of super typhoons that battered the country, and then four years from 2020 because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Frenchman Julien Sale won the revival last year also at the Masters, and he is expected to banner the foreign challenge that will try to prevent a Filipino from again winning since Miguel Tabuena triumphed in the 100th staging at Luisita.

Tabuena, who played in the final season of the now-defunct LIV 1.0 Golf League, and fellow Philippine Asian Games team members Justin delos Santos and Carl Corpus will be on the starting roster, with Tabuena having innate knowledge of one of the local courses he calls home.

That win was the second Open title for Tabuena, who, at 32, has become the face of local pro golf, even as another past champion in Angelo Que is also given an equal chance at 47 years old since he is enjoying one of the finest two-year stretches of his career.
Meanwhile, the management of Manila Southwoods has not stopped in conditioning the Jack Nicklaus-designed Masters since being awarded the rights to host the event for the second straight year.

It will be one of the narrowest versions of the Masters the field will see come the second week of November as the roughs are now being allowed to grow and the fairways reduced in width to punish errant tee shots.
The Asian Tour also did its part in making sure the event goes on as scheduled even after the withdrawal of BingoPlus as the title sponsor.

The online betting app decided to not back the event just over a month ago, threatening to shut down everything before the Asian Tour and the governing National Golf Association of the Philippines pushed all the right buttons to get it going again. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Sara Duterte ex-aide: NBI agents offered me cash, Forbes Park stay
articles.summary: Former Davao City chief information officer Jefry Tupas on Wednesday said National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agents allegedly offered him cash and a place to stay in the upscale Forbes Park in…

blocks.text: Published October 7, 2026 7:17pm

Former Davao City chief information officer Jefry Tupas on Wednesday said National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agents allegedly offered him cash and a place to stay in the upscale Forbes Park in Makati City.

In a statement relayed by his lawyer, Caesar Europa, Tupas said the offer came after authorities supposedly visited him to offer protection amid an alleged threat of abduction by the Dutertes following the cash delivery claims of dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso, Jr.
Tupas said NBI Director Melvin Matibag also assured him that the bureau would protect him and his family.
Europa said Tupas declined the alleged offer.
Tupas has not identified the NBI personnel who allegedly made the offer, nor presented any evidence to substantiate his claim.
It also remains unclear whether the offer of accommodation was meant as a security measure amid an alleged threat against Tupas or was offered as an inducement for his cooperation or testimony.

In a sworn statement, Gracioso had claimed that he delivered suitcases containing cash to Vice President Sara Duterte, Davao City 1st District Rep. Paolo Duterte, and former President Rodrigo Duterte on the supposed instructions of then-House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
He also claimed that Tupas received some of the suitcases on Duterte's behalf.

In a press conference in Davao City on Tuesday, Duterte denied Gracioso's allegations. She also claimed that cash was being offered to individuals to testify about Gracioso's affidavit, citing Tupas' experience.
For his part, Tupas has submitted an affidavit to the NBI denying Gracioso's claims.— MCG, GMA News
